data.claim: Victim item needing the item of the agent waiting on it orders the pair; one edge per cycle suffices
data.falsifier: A 2- or 3-agent ring still showing a cycle or a needs cycle after apply
data.mechanism: The victim yields contested globs and cannot reclaim until the earlier item is done; closure check rules out needs cycles
data.probe: pytest tests/test_conflict_autoorder.py
data.question: Can one needs edge per wait cycle stop the deadlock recurring without creating a needs cycle?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED; ring tests pass
r-lock-cycle-selfheal, r-everything-configurable read; knob schedule.auto_order, CLI config, MCP configure

chunk_findings.detail: `_candidates` treats the two spellings of a link's blocking side as interchangeable in the first loop (`k.get("blocker") == victim_item or victim_item in k.get("blockers", [])`, i.e. a link may legitimately carry only a `blockers` list), but the fallback line unconditionally subscripts `k["blocker"]`. For any cycle whose link dict has only `blockers` (which the first loop explicitly contemplates), `propose` raises `KeyError: 'blocker'` instead of producing edges or a note. Concretely: a cycle dict `{"victim_item": "A", "links": [{"item": "B", "blockers": ["A"]}], "agents": [...], "files": [...]}` causes a crash on `out += [(k["item"], k["blocker"]) for k in links]`, so the self-heal action dies exactly on the input shape the detection code allowed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/autoorder.py:_candidates

chunk_findings.detail: The intent (D-lock-cycle-selfheal, point 3) specifies the default mode as "apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions", i.e. a deadlock cycle must be rewired by default. The documented default here is a single mode `schedule.auto_order = 'propose'`, which only *reports* the edge and never applies it. Under the shipped default, a detected circular wait — the primary trigger of this change — is not repaired, so the unblock the change exists to force never happens unless an operator manually switches to 'apply'. The snapshot text even contradicts itself by calling 'propose' "the strictest" fallback for a deadlock, while the intent treats apply as the required response to a cycle. Either the intent's default is misimplemented or the golden documentation is wrong; as shipped, the feature does not satisfy the recorded requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr:992

chunk_findings.detail: The intent of this change specifies: "the operator can switch the mode: [schedule].auto_order = off | propose | apply (default apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions)". The shipped knob documented in this transcript sets `"schedule.auto_order" = "propose"` as the single default for all triggers, including a detected deadlock cycle. Given a detected wait-for cycle and a project with no explicit config, the effective mode is `propose`, so ddflow only reports the needs edge instead of refilling the tasks and forcing the unblock — exactly the behavior the operator requirement (D-lock-cycle-selfheal: "it must REFILL the tasks with dependencies on each other so the circular waiting cannot recur, and so force the unblock") demands happen by default for a detected cycle. The deadlock therefore recurs on the next collision until a human intervenes, contradicting the filed intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (schedule.auto_order)

chunk_findings.detail: The shipped knob documents `schedule.auto_order = 'propose'` as the single default for every trigger, but the operator directive (D-lock-cycle-selfheal, point 3) mandates "default apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions". The documented default is propose-only with no per-trigger distinction, so under the default configuration a detected circular wait — the case the operator says must be force-unblocked by refilling dependencies — is only reported and the deadlock recurs. The intent and the behavior described by this transcript contradict each other.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (schedule.auto_order entry)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent (D-lock-cycle-selfheal, trigger 2, and the CONFORMANCE note "every number ... a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt") requires a `[schedule].auto_order_wait_s` knob bounding how old a wait may be before auto-order fires. The `--explain` output this transcript pins contains no `schedule.auto_order_wait_s` (nor any wait-age threshold knob) — only `schedule.auto_order`. Either the knob does not exist, in which case the wait-age trigger's number is not configurable as required, or it exists but is undocumented and unpinned by this transcript; both are defects against the stated intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (missing schedule.auto_order_wait_s)

chunk_findings.detail: The knob listing added for the new feature declares `"key": "schedule.auto_order", "value": "propose"` as the default, but the operator intent (D-lock-cycle-selfheal) specifies the default is "apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions". With default `propose`, a detected wait-for cycle — the primary trigger the decision says must force the unblock — writes no `needs` edge and the deadlock can recur indefinitely until a human flips the knob. Either the shipped default contradicts the filed decision, or the decision text does; as recorded data they disagree and the behavior delivered is the weaker one.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (schedule.auto_order)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent and its CONFORMANCE clause require every number of the feature to be a knob, specifically `[schedule].auto_order_wait_s` ("a wait older than [schedule].auto_order_wait_s with nothing running" is trigger 2). The exhaustive `--explain` knob dump in this transcript contains `schedule.auto_order` but no `auto_order_wait_s` (nor any equivalent), so that trigger either does not exist or is governed by a hardcoded, unconfigurable number — violating the stated "every number ... a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (missing schedule.auto_order_wait_s)

data.summary: Upgrade fragments in ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/ are one new file per knob but tasks lease the whole directory (unreleased/*), so a second knob-adding task cannot commit its fragment; fragments should be exempt from leases like pins

data.body:
Fixes bug B92e13a521f: Upgrade fragments in ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/ are one new file per knob but tasks lease the whole directory (unreleased/*), so a second knob-adding task cannot commit its fragment; fragments should be exempt from leases like pins

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B92e13a521f --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B92e13a521f --regression-test <test>` first).

chunk_findings.detail: The shipped knob sets `"propose"` as the single default for all triggers, but the operator directive (D-lock-cycle-selfheal, point 3) mandates "default apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions". The docstring confirms propose only "reports the `needs` edge it would add". Given a detected wait-for cycle in a project with no explicit config, the effective mode is `propose`, so no `needs` edge is written, the circular wait is not rewired, and the unblock this change exists to force never happens until a human flips the knob. The README diff shows the total knob count rising from 269 to exactly 270, and the only schedule-section addition in both the README table and `config_sections/schedule.py` is `schedule.auto_order`. chunk_findings.detail: The intent specifies a per-trigger default mode: "apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions". This function resolves a single mode for the whole call (`mode = mode or cfg.schedule.auto_order`) and applies it uniformly to every entry in `cycles`, which the surrounding design (per intent) can mix: cycle detections, stale waits, and repeated file collisions are all passed in as one `cycles: list[dict]`. With the configurable default `cfg.schedule.auto_order = "apply"`, a run triggered only by repeated undeclared file collisions (e.g. two items repeatedly blocking on a shared pin file) will have its edges written to the log immediately, when the spec says that trigger must default to propose (report only, write nothing). There is no per-cycle/per-trigger mode resolution anywhere in this function, so the documented propose-by-default behavior for the collision trigger cannot occur.

The help text therefore advertises a default mode that contradicts the recorded requirement; a user reading the config help would believe deadlocks are only reported, not rewired, by default.

chunk_findings.detail: The intent states the mode default is "apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions", but this test pins `Config().schedule.auto_order == "propose"` as the single global default, and `test_two_agent_cycle_resolves_in_apply_mode` confirms a detected wait-for cycle does nothing until the operator explicitly runs `config schedule.auto_order apply`.
